title: Incident video-evidence review memorandum - 2024 candidate
summary: A restricted 2024 incident document shows that video footage could be reviewed and summarized in writing as part of an HR/management incident record. The underlying incident facts and identities remain restricted and are not generalized.

claims.claim: A 2024 restricted incident artifact is explicitly a written review of video footage and records the reviewer's observations from the footage.

evidence.note: Underlying incident details and identities are excluded.

claims.claim: The Word document metadata shows the review document was created and modified on the date of the incident review, supporting same-day incident documentation in this example.

evidence.note: Created 2024-08-09; modified later the same day.

trigger: An incident has relevant video footage requiring factual review.
prerequisites: Authorized access to the video evidence.
Incident/case identifier or restricted case location.
steps: Record objective observations and timing/context necessary to the investigation.
Store the written review with the restricted incident/case evidence.
decisions: Whether video is relevant and should be reviewed.
Whether additional evidence/witness follow-up is needed.
controls: Do not generalize the factual allegations or identities from a single incident into policy.
Preserve the original video or source reference separately from the reviewer's narrative.
Distinguish observed video facts from interpretation or conclusions.
Access to video and incident narratives should remain restricted.
unresolved_questions: What current RTEC incident-investigation procedure governs video preservation, access, review, chain of custody and retention?
Is there a standard incident-review form or required reviewer/signoff process?
automation_candidates: Incident evidence manifest that records video source, date/time range, reviewer, review date, hash/reference and resulting memo without embedding private footage in generalized knowledge.
Template separating objective observations from interpretation and follow-up questions.

provenance.notes: Incident identities and factual allegations are excluded from generalized knowledge.
